findings.title: Do not change notification preferences through an authenticated GET
findings.body: The new GET route invokes TopicsController#unsubscribe, which immediately saves a lower notification level for the currently logged-in user. GET requests are not protected by Rails' CSRF token verification, and the action also skips the XHR check. An external site can therefore navigate a logged-in user to this URL and disable their topic notifications without consent. Serve the preference page on GET and perform the mutation through a CSRF-protected POST.

findings.title: Record the unsubscribe as an explicit user preference change
findings.body: Saving notification_level directly leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged, unlike TopicUser.change, which records the user_changed reason. For automatically tracked topics whose reason is still nil, TopicUser.update_last_read automatically sets the level back to tracking once the reading-time threshold is reached. Consequently, a subsequent visit can undo the unsubscribe. Use the normal notification-change mechanism so the explicit preference is preserved.

findings.title: Handle users without an existing TopicUser record
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, but the action unconditionally reads tu.notification_level. The URL is not tied to the email recipient, so a user opening a forwarded email or opening it while logged into another account can have access to the topic without having a TopicUser row. That valid request raises NoMethodError and returns a server error instead of allowing the user to unsubscribe. Create or update the preference through TopicUser.change, which supports missing records.
